title: Payment System Project
content:
Right now I’m finalizing an internal payment system for my company (startup media company). I worked solo on this project with Cursor + Claude

## What I did

I built it as a distributed event-based system composed of domain driven microservices.

Key components

- transaction service which functions as the main integration point and orchestrates various transaction types (payments, transfers, wallet deposits, etc) atomically- Abstracts external payment processors like Stripe/Paypal behind a unified interface- Wallet component (Uber style) for managing user balances within our ecosystem (mobile app, web app)

## Tech stack

- Backed services in Node Typescript- Zod for schema validations- Inversify for dependency injection- NextJS for web client- AWS RDS Postgres- AWS EventBridge + SQS- AWS Elastic Container Service- CI/CD GitHub Actions

## Lessons Learned

I think I should’ve used a Monorepo rather than separate repos for each service

- Easier to build shared components- would have allowed me to feed context more easily and leverage AI better

Utilize gRPC for semi-event-based instead of fully event based

- Would have simplified direct dependent requests between services- Reduce latency

NestJS

- I built a template for my backend node services that included inversifyJS for dependency injection, a custom modular file structure, custom annotations for auth guards- My services were flexible and lightweight but I kindve reinvented Nest in my own way 😂

## Would love some feedback

If you’ve built something similar I’d love to hear what patterns/tools/architecture/workflows worked for you guys

title: Bulletproof MCP calls with `available_tools.xml`
content:
sometimes your coding agents don't listen when you want to reference an MCP.

instead of smacking them, give them more context..

it's an XML file called `[available_tools](https://github.com/Vibe-with-AI/ai-sdlc/blob/agentic/.aisdlc/refs/available-tools.xml)`

I made this by copying the relevant pieces of each MCP's [README.md](http://README.md), then asked an LLM to give me the README's into a format including:

- Available tools- description of tools- tool- tool summary- tool description- tool capabilities- tool function- tool function description- tool paramaters

I attached a snippet in the photos, and provided the full file as a GIST.

## Where do I store this?
.ai/refs/

## How do I use this?
I place it in the user guidelines instructing each request that it has MCP's available, and to reference the `./ai/refs/available_tools.xml` for usage details.

## How do I make my own?
Provide the example from [the example](https://github.com/Vibe-with-AI/ai-sdlc/blob/agentic/.aisdlc/refs/available-tools.xml), copy/paste each [README.md](http://README.md) from the MCP you are using, into the `.ai/refs/mcps`, then ask the LLM to use the `available_tools.xml` as a template, and swap it with the contents of the mcp's you plan to use in `.ai/refs/mcps`

title: Wordpress Vibe Coding - The why and how
content:
Let me share this here hoping it can benefit you if you are also in my situation. I am well versed in WordPress, Drupal, Laravel and a variety of PHP-based CMSes and systems. My Python skills are 1 or 2 out of 10 at the moment (but rising).

When it comes both coding and learning at the same time, it impairs my speed and confidence in the task at hand. @Parker Rex has shared his thoughts on the topic, especially the need for just-in-time and continuous learning. HOWEVER, THE REALITY IS THAT WE HAVE TO BE PRACTICAL AND GROW AT OUR OWN PACE.

If you have clients who wanted your services now, they may not have the patience to wait for you to learn new programming languages.

Most PHP content management systems have built-in ecosystems, plugins, themes, packages, modules that fit the bill for many client websites. There is no need to re-invent the wheel or redo in Python what is freely available on GitHub.

Many people look down on PHP, but my friend Gemini says "PHP is a dominant force on the internet, with a substantial majority of websites relying on this server-side scripting language. As of early to mid-2025, estimates indicate that PHP is used by approximately 74.5% to 80% of all websites whose server-side programming language is known. Some sources suggest that around 77% to 79% of all websites rely on PHP to some degree.

If you come from the PHP community, there is good news. Actually this may apply to other systems like Shopify or social media accounts but let's focus on PHP systems.

You can have your server support both Python and PHP.... then you can code CLI programs to integrate with the CMS. For example if you want to generate images through AI, it might be better to do it in Python and then sync them with your content from the CLI. You can batch create articles, generate data and add content directly to the CMS database, use webhooks to post, or do API integrations.

title: 🔥🔥 Logical 3 Step PRD Prompt Flow (bind these to !f1, !f2, !f3) No Task Master Needed (but its great)
content:
BEFORE YOU START PASTING PROMPTS READ THIS SNIPPET FROM A PREVIOUS POST:

The P in PRD is product. [I made a whole course on product.](https://www.skool.com/troublefreeai/classroom/4ecde1d9?md=af78606ddf5748449b05dc42937cdef7) If you watch it you'll be better at building product. I tried to make it as anti-snooze as possible.

Product strategy happens before you write code.

I follow a simplified format from the book [shape up](https://basecamp.com/shapeup) and have for close to a decade.

- Narrow the problem- Sketch out a few rough solutions to solve said problem- List things out of bounds (no goes)- List potential rabbit holes (things you know could be a time bomb)- Then time box it as a constraint (less relevant - never tell the AI a time box)

It works great for 0 -> 1 and for 1.0 to 1.1 and beyond.

I haven't made videos about this ... but writing it ou,t I realize I should

You get more leverage on your time writing code / designing if you've thought it out ahead of time.

And then you bring it into asking the AI how to further shape your idea, poke holes in it, find open questions, find where it fits into an existing codebase, or where you should start if it's brand new.

What HAS changed drastically is once you're in the editor...
because AI confidently paints a picture of how easy this implementation will be ...then it's 4 am and
You're about to throw your laptop off a bridge.

So it requires having discipline around a set of steps you follow for all work.
If I spent an hour working on a new feature, I'd spend at least half that time refining the PRD. Taking that initial pitch format, researching tech/designs / other people's repos I can learn from. (use search operators like `language:Typescript <concept_you_want_to_learn`

title: Make Rules in Cursor As You Build
content:
Similar to how you should clean as you cook in a kitchen, you should clean your codebase and create rules as you're building. These have a compounding effect on the code quality and the joy you'll get from working in your codebase.

Cursor is incredibly powerful because you can start to create rules around how you'd like things done moving forward. You can select the areas of the codebase that you'd like for these rules to apply to.

I want to cover a couple of the different best practices that I found by digging up Cursor Engineers on X

FAQ:
-----------------

What is an .mdc?

| It's just a markdown file with structured frontmatter that we render a custom editor for so you can @-mention files in yoru codebase and to make sure the metadata stays intact.

Michael also mentioned that the “MDC” in the .mdc file extension means “Markdown Cursor”:

| It means “Markdown Cursor” we just needed a unique extension so we could use the custom editor for these but not for regular markdown files.

Creating rules as you go (taken from Task Master).

-----------------

When should I create a new rule?
Introduce rules when you have new patterns that you want to continue throughout the project. For example, querying data, mutating data, writing components, structuring markdown files, doing external API calls, doing logging, doing traces.

Grab the prompt below and store it in your .cursor/rules/cursor_rules.mdc:

```
---
description: Guidelines for creating and maintaining Cursor rules to ensure consistency and effectiveness.
globs: .cursor/rules/*.mdc
alwaysApply: true
---

- **Required Rule Structure:**
```markdown
---
description: Clear, one-line description of what the rule enforces
globs: path/to/files/*.ext, other/path/**/*
alwaysApply: boolean
---

- **Main Points in Bold**
- Sub-points with details
- Examples and explanations
```

- **File References:**
- Use `\[filename\](mdc:path/to/file)` (\[filename\](mdc:filename)) to reference files
- Example: \[prisma.mdc\](mdc:.cursor/rules/prisma.mdc) for rule references

title: Project-based work system (pls lmk your thoughts)
content:
I tend to (and I know other's in this line of work) tend to work on a project basis. When I'm learning something new, take ML for example, I like to 1. research a bit 2. outline a project with a clear end goal and path which includes all the things I want to learn along the way.

In this example (ML basics), it could be GOAL : 'Working MNIST data classifier (>75% accuracy)'
STACK : 'PyTorch on a Jupyter Notebook, potentially on the platform Kaggle)
STEPS : 1. Set up / understand PyTorch Basics
2. Format dataset...

This is the first-half and most important part. In a way, kind of similar to creating a [plan.md](http://plan.md) for a Cursor build.

Then next step would be to clean up this plan and give it to an LLM to act as my tutor (Google even have a fine-tuned Gemini model for tutoring called LearnLM which I really like).

The V1 of what I'm trying to do is have Agent 1 which works with me on stage 1 (plan formation), potentially via voice for less friction and more data input/s. And then have the plan structured in a DB for the Tutor agent / agent team to reference.

Key part for long term is to build an app that can manage the data associated with your progress in the project, i.e. your notes, thoughts, struggles, actual code...

Find a way to context cache it effectively and use as LLM context for longer projects.
Long-term I'd like to have an Obsidian style DB of all the content of my learning which can be used as 'smart-context'.

What problem does it solve?
LLM driven learning is highly segmented and many people use multiple tools in a single learning-project workflow.

How long have I been working on it?
Been experimenting with prototyping different parts of it over the past 2 months.

What technologies does it use?
It’s a web app built using probs Next.Js ,OAI Agents SDK in the backend, and a combo of Supabase and PostreSQL (although I'm still looking into it, was using Pinecone for Vector stuff before).

Been prototyping the agent workflows in Relevance AI / N8n / Make.

title: Introduce Yourself! (Start Here!!)
For Coders: Cursor Memory Bank (Inspired by Cline) Is The Best Flow I've Used EVER.
content:
In case you missed it, I've spoken at length about Cline and its place in AI Coding tools.

It consistently leads the pack in innovating patterns that the rest of the SaaS products fast-follow.

They recently launched Memory Bank, a pattern that continually provides your coding agent with context.

It is fantastic.

Yet if you already use Cursor, it's better to save $$$ on tokens and bring that set of instructions over.

Here's the article on how it works:
[https://docs.cline.bot/improving-your-prompting-skills/custom-instructions-library/cline-memory-bank](https://docs.cline.bot/improving-your-prompting-skills/custom-instructions-library/cline-memory-bank)

The docs are a bit confusing so I'll summarize.

[ol:1]- Take the Custom Instructions from that article- Paste them into the User Instructions section in Cursor (accessed by Cursor Settings)- Create a new folder called memory-bank- Create a new file in that folder called [project-brief.md](http://project-brief.md)- [project-brief.md](http://project-brief.md) will be the source of truth for whatever you are working on.- Fill out your [project-brief.md](http://project-brief.md) with specifics on what you are trying to get done- Include snippets, examples, documentation on the task at hand. If its a bug, classify it as such. - Open Cursor Agent mode, and add [project-brief.md](http://project-brief.md) to context- Type "Read your User Instructions"- Cursor reads the instructions, reads the brief, and creates the files necessary to hold your memory bank. 

I used this for 6 hours yesterday.

It rendered far better results than anything I've ever tested.

Keep in mind: Prompts are only 80% if you don't know how to do the task you are asking AI to complete.
Your knowledge has a multiple on it with AI. Your lack of knowledge has a token multiple on it -- aka it'll be more expensive in cost and time if you spam AI without specifics.

so i typically would research them...

watch videos

take notes...

and thats still valuable no doubt

but i wanted to see how far i could push ai using a few different tools

because the output of what i want to learn is pretty much the same for any entrepreneur

what i want to know
[ol:1]- what niche did they start in- what niche are they in now- how long did it take them to get to where they are now- what tactics did they do each year, and what amount of $$$ did they generate during that period- what are the SPECIFIC daily actions they took.. eg. SEO & Content planning isnt helpful.. 5x 1,000-1,500 word keyword-researched listicle-style blog posts + reaching out to high domain authority ranking sites in their niche is helpful- if you cant find the specifics of the tactic in the youtube video, go research using web - timeline of their growth over time

btw in ai/tech world this is known as structured json output which gives the ai a set of instructions it needs to fill out in order to complete its job
